dialogue.content: こんにちは。
dialogue.English: Hello.

dialogue.content: カウンセラー役のジンと申します。今日はどうぞよろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: My name is Jin, and I'll be your counselor today. It's a pleasure to meet you.

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします！
dialogue.English: It's a pleasure to meet you too!

dialogue.content: 早速ですが、どのようなご相談か伺ってもよろしいですか？
dialogue.English: To begin, may I ask what brings you in today?

dialogue.content: 会社の隣の後輩がうるさくて困ってます
dialogue.English: I’m having trouble because the junior colleague who sits next to me at work is so loud.

dialogue.content: 隣の後輩がうるさくて困っていらっしゃるんですね。
dialogue.English: So, you're troubled by your loud junior colleague who sits next to you.

dialogue.content: 注意はできないし、
dialogue.English: I can't bring myself to say anything about it,

dialogue.content: 注意できないんですね。
dialogue.English: It feels difficult to address it directly.

dialogue.content: 会社行くのが憂鬱なんです
dialogue.English: It makes me dread going to work.

dialogue.content: そうなんです
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: かなり、お辛いんですね。
dialogue.English: That sounds very difficult for you.

dialogue.content: 辛いですね
dialogue.English: It is difficult.

dialogue.content: お困りだと思います。
dialogue.English: I can imagine how troubling that must be.

dialogue.content: 頭にガンガン響くくらいうるさくて・・・
dialogue.English: It's so loud it feels like it's pounding in my head...

dialogue.content: 頭に響く・・・それは相当ですね。
dialogue.English: Pounding in your head... that sounds quite severe.

dialogue.content: うるさいんですー
dialogue.English: It's just so loud!

dialogue.content: 声が大きいのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is their voice very loud?

dialogue.content: そうです！声もでかく、ベラベラ喋ってて
dialogue.English: Yes! A booming voice, and they chatter on and on.

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: よろしければもっとお聞かせください。
dialogue.English: If you’re comfortable, please tell me more.

dialogue.content: 今年の4月の人事異動で隣にきた女子社員です。
dialogue.English: She's a female employee who moved next to me during the personnel changes this past April.

dialogue.content: 体も大きく、声もでかく、
dialogue.English: She has a large build and a loud voice,

dialogue.content: 今年、4月からなんですね。体も、声も大きいんですね。それは気になりますね。
dialogue.English: So, this started in April. And she has a large build and a loud voice. I can see why that would be distracting.

dialogue.content: わちゃわちゃ騒いでて、大した仕事してないんですが、
dialogue.English: She's always making a commotion, and she doesn't seem to be doing much important work, but...

dialogue.content: 騒いでいる感じなんですか。
dialogue.English: It feels like she's making a commotion?

dialogue.content: 話しかたが上手いので、仕事できる人、と見えなくもなく、評価は高いみたいですー
dialogue.English: She's a smooth talker, so she comes across as capable, and it seems she's well-regarded.

dialogue.content: それも悔しい感じですが
dialogue.English: That’s frustrating too.

dialogue.content: それはモヤモヤしますね。
dialogue.English: That must leave you feeling unsettled.

dialogue.content: 一番は、声がうるさく、仕事の邪魔です
dialogue.English: The biggest problem is that her voice is loud and it disrupts my work.

dialogue.content: もーーーー思い出すだけで、怒りが・・・
dialogue.English: Ugh, just thinking about it makes me angry...

dialogue.content: わかります。気になって仕方ないですよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. It must be impossible to ignore.

dialogue.content: 他の職場の皆さんはどのような感じなのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: How do the others in the workplace feel about it?

dialogue.content: 元気な人として接してます
dialogue.English: They treat her like she's just an energetic person.

dialogue.content: 本音は煩い、ウザいと思ってるはずですが、
dialogue.English: I'm sure they actually find her loud and annoying, but...

dialogue.content: みんな笑って済ませてます
dialogue.English: Everyone just laughs it off.

dialogue.content: そのうちブチ切れそうです
dialogue.English: I feel like I'm going to snap soon.

dialogue.content: ああ、本音はうざがっていても、表面的には笑って済ませているんですね。
dialogue.English: Ah, so even though they're annoyed, on the surface, they just laugh it off.

dialogue.content: ブチ切れたら会社はクビになっちゃうと思う・・・
dialogue.English: If I snap, I think I'll get fired...

dialogue.content: ストレスがたまりますね。
dialogue.English: That must be very stressful.

dialogue.content: 法律で守ってもらえないんですかー？
dialogue.English: Isn’t there any legal protection for me?

dialogue.content: それで、相談者様がクビになってはたまったものではないですね。法律については詳しくないのですが、管理者には職場環境をよくする義務があります。
dialogue.English: It would be terrible if you were the one to be fired over this. I'm not an expert on the law, but managers do have a duty to maintain a healthy work environment.

dialogue.content: 相談者様の管理者は相談に乗ってはくれないでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Would your manager be open to discussing this with you?

dialogue.content: そうそれ！！
dialogue.English: That's the thing!!

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 元気でいいね言ってます
dialogue.English: They say things like, "It's great she's so energetic."

dialogue.content: 管理者が、肯定的に受け止めてしまっているんですね。
dialogue.English: So your manager sees it as a positive thing.

dialogue.content: それはますますストレスがたまると思います。
dialogue.English: That must make it even more stressful.

dialogue.content: そうみたい
dialogue.English: It seems so.

dialogue.content: 職場に、他に、相談できる方はいらっしゃらないでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is there anyone else at work you could talk to?

dialogue.content: いっぱいいるけど、みんな同じ気持ちだと思う
dialogue.English: There are plenty of people, but I think they all feel the same way.

dialogue.content: 相談者様の気持ちをわかってくれる人がいないのは、なお辛いと思います。
dialogue.English: It must be even harder when you feel there's no one who understands how you feel.

dialogue.content: みんな同じ気持ちでいて、でも我慢してる感じです
dialogue.English: It feels like everyone feels the same, but they’re just putting up with it.

dialogue.content: よろしければ、どのような職場なのかお聞かせいただけますか？
dialogue.English: If you don't mind, could you tell me a little about your workplace?

dialogue.content: 課長も部長も苦笑いしてるから、私たちの気持ちは察してるんだとおもいます
dialogue.English: The section chief and department head are giving wry smiles, so I think they sense how we feel.

dialogue.content: 行き違いました。みなさん我慢してらっしゃるんですね。
dialogue.English: My apologies, I misunderstood. So everyone is just enduring it.

dialogue.content: 課長も部長もみんな我慢してるのは知ってると思います
dialogue.English: I think the section chief and department head know everyone is putting up with it.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。しかし状況は変わらないんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. But the situation isn't changing.

dialogue.content: でも、多分、病気なのかもしれません。もしかしたら、耳の病気か？？
dialogue.English: But, maybe she has some kind of illness. Perhaps an ear condition?

dialogue.content: 耳の病気かもしれないんですね。
dialogue.English: So you’re wondering if it could be a hearing condition.

dialogue.content: すごく太ってるんですね、ダイエットする気もないみたいで、
dialogue.English: She's very overweight, and doesn't seem to have any intention of dieting.

dialogue.content: それも病気なのかもしれません。
dialogue.English: That might be due to an illness too.

dialogue.content: そんな状況で、あんたうるさいから黙れちは言えません
dialogue.English: In that situation, I can't just tell her, "You're loud, so shut up."

dialogue.content: なるほど
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: しかし、はっきりしないでただ我慢するのも辛いですよね。
dialogue.English: However, just putting up with it without any clarity must be difficult.

dialogue.content: 何か、解決策がないか、一緒に考えたいと思います。
dialogue.English: I'd like to think together with you to see if we can find some kind of solution.

dialogue.content: どうすればいいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What should I do?

dialogue.content: 職場の管理職が相談にのってくれないとのことでしたが、会社には職場の悩み事を聞いてくれるような窓口はないでしょうか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned your manager isn't receptive, but does your company have a support desk or a contact person for workplace concerns?

dialogue.content: ないです
dialogue.English: No, there isn't.

dialogue.content: なるほど。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: では、相談者様の職場には、産業医の先生はいらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.English: In that case, does your workplace have an occupational physician?

dialogue.content: いないとおもいます
dialogue.English: I don't think so.

dialogue.content: そうですか。もしいらっしゃれば、と思ったのですが。
dialogue.English: I see. I was thinking that could be an option if there were one.

dialogue.content: 会社の隣に内科はありますが・・・
dialogue.English: There’s an internal medicine clinic next to the company...

dialogue.content: はい。健康診断などを担当していらっしゃる先生であれば、相談できるかもしれません。
dialogue.English: I see. If it's a doctor who handles things like company health check-ups, you might be able to consult with them.

dialogue.content: 会社とは関係ない内科医院だと思います
dialogue.English: I think it's just an unrelated internal medicine clinic.

dialogue.content: なるほど。やはり、職場内で、できることを考えてみたほうが良さそうです。
dialogue.English: I understand. In that case, it seems best to think about what can be done within the workplace.

dialogue.content: ご相談の最初の方で、「本人に注意できない」とおっしゃっていましたが、どうしてそう思われるのでしょうか？　やはりご病気の可能性があるからでしょうか？
dialogue.English: At the beginning of our session, you mentioned you "can't say anything to her." Why do you feel that way? Is it because you suspect she might have a health condition?

dialogue.content: それもあるし、言ったらキマづくなるし、言っても口答えしてくると思うし、
dialogue.English: That's part of it, but also it would make things awkward, and I think she would just talk back.

dialogue.content: それやったらもう一生話しないと思う
dialogue.English: If that happened, I don't think we'd ever speak again.

dialogue.content: 口答えですか、それはやりづらいですね。
dialogue.English: She would talk back? That would certainly make things difficult.

dialogue.content: 職場は何人ぐらいで働いていらっしゃるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: About how many people work in your office?

dialogue.content: 全部で10人です
dialogue.English: There are 10 of us in total.

dialogue.content: なるほど。例えば、席替えなどで離れられた少しはましになる感じでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. For example, do you think it would be a little better if you could move seats?

dialogue.content: 席替えはないですね、固定されてます。
dialogue.English: We don’t change seats; they’re fixed.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 別な人が犠牲者なります
dialogue.English: Someone else would just become the next victim.

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: That’s true.

dialogue.content: そんなにみんなが困っているのに、管理職が話を聞いてくれないのは困りますね。
dialogue.English: It's problematic that your manager won't listen when so many people are having trouble.

dialogue.content: 管理職に対応をしてもらう方法があればいいんですが・・
dialogue.English: I wish there were a way to get management to take action...

dialogue.content: 課長はその子の中まで、よくランチ行ったり、飲み会したり、休日も焼き肉パーティしたりしてるみたいです
dialogue.English: The section chief seems close with her—they often go out to lunch and to drinking parties, and even have barbecue parties on days off.

dialogue.content: 仲間  です
dialogue.English: They’re buddies.

dialogue.content: 私も、飲み会は半分は行ってます。
dialogue.English: I go to about half of the drinking parties myself.

dialogue.content: そうですか。飲み会ではどんな感じなのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. What is she like at these drinking parties?

dialogue.content: ランチは、気がくるいそうなるので断ってます
dialogue.English: I turn down lunch because I feel like I’d go crazy.

dialogue.content: 一人でガーーガーー喋ってます
dialogue.English: She just drones on and on by herself.

dialogue.content: 1人でガーガー・・他のみなさんもストレスを感じておられることと思います。
dialogue.English: Droning on by herself... I imagine your other colleagues must be stressed as well.

dialogue.content: 嵐のファンで、いっつも嵐の話です
dialogue.English: She's a fan of Arashi, and she's always talking about them.

dialogue.content: 嵐ファンですか。熱狂的なイメージがします。
dialogue.English: A fan of Arashi? I can imagine she's very enthusiastic.

dialogue.content: みんな迷惑してる思います。迷惑おばさんです
dialogue.English: I think everyone is annoyed. She's a nuisance.

dialogue.content: 他の職場の皆さんは我慢しているとのことですが、この問題を話し合われたことはおありでしょうか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned your colleagues are putting up with it, but have you ever discussed this issue with them?

dialogue.content: ないかな・・・そんな雰囲気もないですね
dialogue.English: I don't think so... it's not really the kind of atmosphere for it.

dialogue.content: そうですか。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: ここまでのお話を一度まとめさせていただいてもよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Would it be all right if I took a moment to summarize what we've discussed so far?

dialogue.content: はーいどうぞー
dialogue.English: Sure, go ahead.

dialogue.content: 相談者様は、隣の席の女性社員の話し声がうるさくて切れそうになるほど困っていらっしゃる。
dialogue.English: You're troubled by the loud voice of the female colleague sitting next to you, to the point where you feel you might snap.

dialogue.content: しかし、相談すべき管理職は、その女性社員と仲が良いので、相談には乗ってくれそうにない。
dialogue.English: However, the manager you would normally consult is friends with her, so it doesn't seem like he would be receptive to your concerns.

dialogue.content: このままではブチ切れて、自分がクビになってしまわないか心配だ。
dialogue.English: You're worried that if this continues, you might snap and end up getting fired yourself.

dialogue.content: このような感じでしょうか？違和感があればおっしゃってください。
dialogue.English: Does that sound about right? Please let me know if anything feels off.

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です
dialogue.English: That's correct.

dialogue.content: はい。そこで少し思ったことを話させていただいてもよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. May I share a few thoughts?

dialogue.content: どうぞー
dialogue.English: Please do.

dialogue.content: 相談者様は、真剣に仕事に取り組んでおられるとお見受けしました。
dialogue.English: It seems to me you take your work very seriously.

dialogue.content: それが邪魔されてしまうのはとてもお辛いことと思います。
dialogue.English: It must be very distressing to have that disrupted.

dialogue.content: おそらく、職場の同僚の方も同じようにお困りだと思います。そこで、一度、同僚の方と相談されてみてはいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I imagine your colleagues are probably struggling with this as well. With that in mind, how about trying to talk with your colleagues about it first?

dialogue.content: その上で、何人かで、管理職の方に、訴えて見るのはどうでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Then, perhaps several of you could approach your manager together?

dialogue.content: 相談ですかうるさくて困ってないか聞いてみます
dialogue.English: Consult with them? You mean ask if they’re also bothered by the noise? I'll give it a try.

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 管理職の方に訴えるのは、少し勇気がいることだと思いますが、1人より何人か味方がいたほうが心強いと思います。
dialogue.English: Approaching your manager might take some courage, but I think it would be more reassuring to have a few allies with you than to go alone.

dialogue.content: やってみますね
dialogue.English: I’ll give it a try.

dialogue.content: はい。管理職には、職場環境をよくする義務があるので、切実さが伝われば、きっと何か対応をしてくれるのではないかと思います。
dialogue.English: Yes. Managers have a duty to maintain a good work environment, so if you can convey the seriousness of the situation, I believe they will surely take some action.

dialogue.content: わかりましたー
dialogue.English: I understand.

dialogue.content: 相談者様のお悩みは、会社の業績にもつながることだと思うので、理解を得られるのではないかと思います。
dialogue.English: I also think your concern ties to the company's productivity and performance, so you may be able to gain their understanding.

dialogue.content: そうですか
dialogue.English: Do you think so?

dialogue.content: はい。そう思います。
dialogue.English: Yes, I do.

dialogue.content: お話を通して、相談者様が職場を大切に考えてらっしゃることが伝わってきました。その思いはきっと管理職にも伝わると思います。
dialogue.English: Throughout our conversation, it's become clear to me that you care a great deal about your workplace. I'm sure that feeling will get through to your manager as well.

dialogue.content: はいわかりました
dialogue.English: Yes, I understand.

dialogue.content: そろそろお時間が近づいてきたのですが、他にご相談はありますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Our time is almost up. Is there anything else you'd like to discuss?

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です
dialogue.English: No, I'm okay.

dialogue.content: では、ここで終了とさせていただきます。本日は大変ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Then, we'll conclude our session here. Thank you very much for your time today.

dialogue.content: ありがとございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you.
